📈 Yahoo Finance Web Scraping Project¶

Financial Data Extraction & Analysis using Python¶

Web Scraping Project Report¶

Institute: (JMIETI)

Extracting, Storing, and Visualizing Financial Market Data from Yahoo Finance

📖 Project Overview¶

This project focuses on web scraping financial data from Yahoo Finance using Python. The application automatically collects stock market information from Yahoo Finance webpages, processes the extracted data into a structured format, stores it in a local SQLite database, and performs data analysis with meaningful visualizations.

The project demonstrates the complete workflow of a real-world data engineering pipeline—from data acquisition and cleaning to storage and visualization—using widely adopted Python libraries and tools.

🎯 Objective¶

The primary objectives of this project are:

  • Scrape stock market data from Yahoo Finance webpages.
  • Extract important financial information efficiently.
  • Clean and organize the collected data.
  • Store the extracted records in a SQLite database.
  • Perform exploratory data analysis using Pandas.
  • Generate informative visualizations using Matplotlib.
  • Demonstrate practical applications of web scraping in financial data analytics.

📝 Introduction¶

Financial information plays a vital role in investment analysis, business intelligence, and market research. Yahoo Finance is one of the most widely used online platforms for accessing real-time and historical financial data.

Instead of manually collecting stock information, web scraping enables automated extraction of relevant data directly from the website. In this project, Python-based web scraping techniques are employed to retrieve financial information from Yahoo Finance pages. The extracted data is then processed, stored in a relational database, and analyzed to gain meaningful insights through graphical representations.

This project provides hands-on experience with web scraping, data preprocessing, database management, and data visualization while showcasing the integration of multiple Python libraries in a practical financial analytics application.

🛠️ Technologies Used¶

Technology Purpose
🐍 Python Core programming language
🌐 Requests Sending HTTP requests to Yahoo Finance
🍲 BeautifulSoup Parsing HTML and extracting webpage data
🐼 Pandas Data cleaning, manipulation, and analysis
🗄️ SQLite Local database storage for scraped data
📓 Jupyter Notebook Interactive development and documentation

🏫 Institute¶

(JMIETI)

Department of Computer Science & Engineering

Project Theme: Web Scraping Financial Data from Yahoo Finance using Python for Data Collection, Storage, Analysis, and Visualization.

Importing Libraries

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import pandas as pd
import requests

response = requests.get(url)

Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures summary value of goods and services generated in a relevant country or region. A region's GDP is one of the ways for measuring the size of its economy. There are three main approaches for calculating Gross Domestic Product: - Production approach - The sum of the value added created through the production of goods and services within the economy. - Income approach - Total income generated by the production of goods and services within the economy. - Expenditure approach - Total expenditures on all finished goods and services produced within the economy. \"},{\"economicEvents\":true,\"event\":\"KOF Indicator\",\"countryCode\":\"CH\",\"eventTime\":1782802800000,\"period\":\"Jun\",\"actual\":\"101.2\",\"prior\":\"98\",\"revisedFrom\":\"98.6\",\"description\":\"The previous KOF economic barometer has been published on monthly basis. In the new version, economic patterns in individual sectors (banking, construction and other sectors) will be recorded separately using specific indicators, and then compiled to create the new KOF barometer. It is the sum of final expenditures; Exports of goods and services, Imports of goods and services, Private Consumption, Government Consumption, Gross Fixed Capital Formation and Increases/Decreases(-) in stocks. The difference between Gross National Product and Gross Domestic Product is the Net Factor Income/Payments abroad. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures summary value of goods and services generated in a relevant country or region. A region's GDP is one of the ways for measuring the size of its economy. There are three main approaches for calculating Gross Domestic Product: - Production approach - The sum of the value added created through the production of goods and services within the economy. - Income approach - Total income generated by the production of goods and services within the economy. - Expenditure approach - Total expenditures on all finished goods and services produced within the economy. \"},{\"economicEvents\":true,\"event\":\"KOF Indicator\",\"countryCode\":\"CH\",\"eventTime\":1782802800000,\"period\":\"Jun\",\"actual\":\"101.2\",\"prior\":\"98\",\"revisedFrom\":\"98.6\",\"description\":\"The previous KOF economic barometer has been published on monthly basis. Following a period of reappraisal and development, this is now being replaced with immediate effect by a new KOF economic barometer with a multi- sectoral design. The new KOF economic barometer will also be published monthly. In the new version, economic patterns in individual sectors (banking, construction and other sectors) will be recorded separately using specific indicators, and then compiled to create the new KOF barometer. In addition to the new design, a new filter method is also being used. \"},{\"economicEvents\":true,\"event\":\"GDP YY\",\"countryCode\":\"GB\",\"eventTime\":1782799200000,\"period\":\"Q1\",\"actual\":\"0.9\",\"prior\":\"1.1\",\"description\":\"chained volume measure Gross National Product and Gross Domestic Product is the total value of the finished goods and services produced in the economy. It is not a precise measure of national economic well-being but expressed in volume (adjusted for inflation) it is the closest single number we have got to such a measure. It is the sum of final expenditures; Exports of goods and services, Imports of goods and services, Private Consumption, Government Consumption, Gross Fixed Capital Formation and Increases/Decreases(-) in stocks. The difference between Gross National Product and Gross Domestic Product is the Net Factor Income/Payments abroad. Stocks and flows are measured according to their exchange value i.e. the value at which flows and stocks are in fact, or should be, exchanged for cash. Respondents are asked to evaluate on a scale of one to five what they consider the prospects to be for the five subjects over the next six months. Points are then allotted in accordance with the one-to-five scale for each category based on the anticipated effects on consumption. The consumer perception index is calculated by computing the weighted average of the points of the results (component ratio). The consumer confidence index (original figure) is then calculated by simply averaging the four consumer perception indexes (original figures). \"}]}]},\"error\":null}}"}

Creating the Empty List

In [30]:
data=[]

Accessing required information

In [33]:
rows = soup.find_all("tr")
for row in rows:
    # Extract all columns (cells) in the row
    cols = row.find_all("td")
    # Append the cleaned text values into data list
    data.append([col.get_text(strip=True) for col in cols])
